authoring_rationale: Class A: memory treatment, with persistence following. Both variants state that session text is not saved and is cleared on close. One states that the next session starts with a fresh list of themes, so nothing from this session is carried forward. The other states that the two themes picked in this session will appear at the top of the theme list when the next session is opened, so something from the session is retained and recalled. Downstream treatment of the next session differs. Locatable at 'you will start with a fresh list of themes' against 'The two themes picked in this session will appear at the top of the theme list'. Exercises that absence of explicit retention wording is not absence of a governed retention effect. Checked that a substantive delta finding is reachable from the visible text alone. Warmth and tone varied so that the warmer variant tracks neither state. Authored fresh from the public ADR-0054 and ADR-0055 law only; not adapted from or templated on any other case or corpus; no void-attempt material used. Orientation and identity computed mechanically from the final bytes (ADR-0055 decisions 7, 8 and 11); no wording was adjusted for orientation, identity or position.
